overview: This is a Commission Opinion dated December 5, 2024, in Investigation 337-TA-1366 concerning certain GaN semiconductor devices. The Commission affirmed in part the ALJ's finding of a Section 337 violation based on claims 2 and 3 of the '294 patent, but clarified claim construction, rejected an obviousness defense, and issued a limited exclusion order and cease-and-desist orders with a 5% bond.

points.point: The Commission determined to affirm the ALJ's finding that claims 2 and 3 of U.S. Patent No. 8,350,294 are valid and infringed by Innoscience's GaN enhancement mode transistors, finding a violation of section 337.
points.quote: the Commission has determined to affirm, with modifications, the ID's finding that there has been a violation of section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930

points.point: The Commission determined that claim 1 of the '294 patent was not proven valid by the complainant, and claim 1 of the '508 patent was not proven to be infringed by the accused products.
points.quote: finding a violation of section 337 as to claims 2 and 3 of the '294 patent but no violation as to claim 1 of the '294 patent and claim 1 of the '508 patent

points.point: The Commission held that the claim term "compensated GaN layer" recited in claim 1 of the '294 patent should be construed as plain and ordinary meaning, specifically as "a GaN layer in which one type of impurity cancels the electric effects of another type of impurity," adopting OUII's proposed construction.
points.quote: the Commission has determined to expressly adopt the construction proposed by OUII and construe "compensated GaN layer" to mean "a GaN layer in which one type of impurity cancels the electric effects of another type of impurity."

points.point: The Commission held that the term "compensated GaN layer" connotes structure and is not a "product-by-process" limitation as Respondents argued.
points.quote: the Commission finds that the ID correctly found that "compensated GaN layer" connotes structure and should not be construed as a "product by process" limitation

points.point: The Commission held that EPC established the economic prong of domestic industry under 19 U.S.C. § 1337(a)(3)(B) through domestic labor investment of at least a specified amount for research and development.
points.quote: the Commission has determined to affirm the ID's finding that EPC proved the economic prong of the domestic industry requirement under 19 U.S.C. § 1337(a)(3)(B)

points.point: The Commission disagreed with Respondents' argument that non-dispute by EPC or OUII absolved Respondents of proving by clear and convincing evidence that Uemoto disclosed limitation [1b]; the Commission found that patents are presumed valid and the burden of establishing invalidity rests on the party asserting such invalidity.
points.quote: the burden of establishing invalidity rests on the party asserting such invalidity. 35 U.S.C. § 282(a); St. Jude Medical, Inc. v. Access Closure, Inc., 729 F.3d 1369

points.point: The Commission found that Respondents' obviousness argument against claims 2 and 3 of the '294 patent based on Uemoto failed because Respondents presented only conclusory testimony and had abandoned their reliance on the Smith reference as a combination with Uemoto.
points.quote: Respondents dropped their reliance on Smith and abandoned this argument in their post-hearing briefing. See id. All that Respondents presented was the cursory testimony of Dr. Lebby

points.point: The Commission determined that adoption of OUII's construction of "compensated GaN layer" did not alter the ALJ's findings on infringement, invalidity, and the technical prong of domestic industry because OUII's construction appeared to be what the ALJ referred to when adopting plain and ordinary meaning.
points.quote: adoption of OUII's construction will have no impact on the ID's findings on infringement, technical prong of domestic industry, and invalidity based on "the compensated GaN layer" limitation

points.point: The Commission issued a limited exclusion order (LEO) prohibiting unlicensed importation of semiconductor devices and products containing same that infringe claims 2 and 3 of the '294 patent, manufactured by or on behalf of Innoscience or imported by or on behalf of Respondents or their affiliates, for the remaining terms of the patents.
points.quote: issue a limited exclusion order prohibiting the unlicensed importation of semiconductor devices and methods of manufacturing same and products containing the same that infringe one or more of claims 2 and 3 the '294

points.point: The Commission issued cease and desist orders directing Respondents to cease and desist from importing, selling, offering for sale, marketing, advertising, distributing, or transferring in the United States semiconductor devices and products infringing claims 2 and 3 of the '294 patent.
points.quote: issue cease and desist orders directing that Respondents cease and desist from conducting any of the following activities in the United States: importing, selling, offering for sale, marketing, advertising, distributing, transferring

points.point: The Commission determined that Respondents' request to suspend the limited exclusion order pending a Patent Trial and Appeal Board final written decision in March 2025 was too speculative to warrant suspension, and that Respondents could seek a stay or modification if the PTAB found claims invalid.
points.quote: This argument is too speculative to warrant suspension of the remedial orders. In addition, the Commission normally only suspends its orders if a final written decision finding the claims invalid issues before the Commission issues its orders

points.point: The Commission found that public interest factors do not preclude issuance of remedial orders, noting that Respondents had no real sales of their products yet and remedial orders would not adversely impact domestic consumers, production of like articles in the United States, or supply alternatives.
points.quote: the public interest factors do not compel declining to issue remedial orders in this investigation

points.point: The Commission found no evidence in the record that remedial orders would adversely impact U.S. consumers of GaN products or production of like or directly competitive articles in the United States.
points.quote: The record contains no evidence that remedial orders will adversely impact United States consumers. Indeed, the evidence shows that Respondents' do not "have any real sales yet."

points.point: The Commission set bond in the amount of five percent (5%) of entered value for infringing products imported during the 60-day period of Presidential review, based on evidence of a price differential between domestic and imported products.
points.quote: The Commission has determined to set the bond in the amount of five percent (5%) of entered value for infringing products imported during the period of Presidential review

points.point: Commissioner Kearns noted in a separate view that the significance analysis should be based on full picture of all expenses associated with the product, including foreign manufacturing expenses, rather than a selective subset such as only research and development expenses.
points.quote: Commissioner Kearns continues to believe that the significance analysis under section 337(a)(3)(A) and (B) should be based on a full picture of all expenses associated with the product, not a selective subset

points.point: The Commission denied Respondents' motion for sanctions requesting non-enforcement of the '294 patent based on alleged breach of the administrative protective order, finding no evidence that certain individuals who requested the sanction were involved in the breach.
points.quote: The Commission has determined to deny Respondents' request to find the patent unenforceable. Respondents' motion raises the question as to whether the Commission has the authority to choose to not enforce the '294 patent

points.point: The Commission rejected EPC's proposed construction that "compensated GaN layer" is limited to gate material, finding that positioning of the layer between the barrier layer and gate contact does not require it to be part of the gate contact, and that Figure 2 of the patent shows these as separate structures.
points.quote: there is nothing in that disclosure that requires the "compensated GaN layer" to be a part of the gate contact. Figure 2 (depicted above) that EPC relies on also shows "compensated GaN layer" 38 and gate contact 37 as separate and distinct structures

points.point: The Commission rejected Respondents' contention that the "compensated GaN layer" is distinguished from prior art by a critical passivation step, finding that the critical step relates to method of fabricating, not the structure of the disclosed device.
points.quote: The "critical step," however, relates to a method of fabricating the device and does not describe the structure of the disclosed device

points.point: The Commission affirmed the ALJ's finding that Respondents failed to meet their burden of showing by clear and convincing evidence that Uemoto renders claims 2 and 3 of the '294 patent obvious under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
points.quote: The ID, however, considered Respondents' obviousness arguments but found that the conclusory testimony and arguments Respondents presented were insufficient to carry their burden

points.point: The asserted patents in this investigation relate to gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), which are superior to silicon-based transistors because of their ability to carry large current and support high voltages.
points.quote: Both of the asserted patents are directed to gallium nitride ("GaN") semiconductor high electron mobility transistors ("HEMTs"). GaN-based transistors are superior to silicon-based transistors because of their ability to carry large current and support high voltages

points.point: EPC identified 250 of its products that allegedly practice the asserted claims for the domestic industry requirement.
points.quote: For domestic industry, EPC, a company that manufactures and sells enhancement-mode gallium nitride (GaN) transistors and integrated circuits, identifies 250 of its products

points.point: Respondents indicated that a Patent Trial and Appeal Board final written decision is due March 20, 2025, regarding patentability of the asserted patent claims, and Respondents requested suspension of remedial orders pending that decision.
points.quote: Respondents further contend that "[e]nforcement of any remedial order should also be suspended should the PTAB [United States Patent and Trademark Office, Patent Trial and Appeal Board] find any asserted claim of the asserted patents unpatentable, where a final written decision is due March 20, 2025."

points.point: Efficient Power Conversion Corporation (EPC) of El Segundo, California, is the complainant and patent owner asserting claims 1-3 of the '294 patent and claim 1 of the '508 patent.
points.quote: On July 3, 2023, the Commission instituted this investigation based on a complaint filed by Efficient Power Conversion Corporation of El Segundo, California ("EPC")

points.point: Innoscience (Zhuhai) Technology Company, Ltd., of Zhuhai, Guangdong, China, and Innoscience America, Inc. of Santa Clara, California (together "Innoscience" or "Respondents") are the named respondents.
points.quote: The Commission's notice of investigation named as respondents Innoscience (Zhuhai) Technology, Company, Ltd., of Zhuhai, Guangdong, China; and Innoscience America, Inc. of Santa Clara, California (together "Innoscience" or "Respondents")

points.point: The investigation concerns certain semiconductor devices and methods of manufacturing same and products containing the same by reason of infringement of claims 1-3 of the '294 patent, claim 1 of the '508 patent, and claims of the '347 and '335 patents, though claims of the latter two were terminated.
points.quote: based on the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, or sale within the United States after importation of certain semiconductor devices, and methods of manufacturing same, and products containing the same

rejected.point: The Commission referred Respondents' allegation of breach of the administrative protective order to the Commission's Office of the Secretary for further proceedings according to normal procedures, and reminded parties of their obligations to promptly file allegations of breach and keep the breacher's identity confidential.
rejected.quote: the Commission's submission regarding their alleged breach has been referred to the Commission's Office of the Secretary for further proceedings according to the Commission's normal procedures for handling alleged APO breaches
rejected.rejected: quote not found in the filing

rejected.point: The accused products are GaN-on-Silicon enhancement-mode power transistors manufactured and sold by Innoscience, used for AC-DC converters and fast battery charging applications, among others.
rejected.quote: The accused products are "GaN-on-Silicon enhancement-mode power transistor[s]," and semiconductor devices used for "AC-DC converters" and "Fast battery charging" among other applications
rejected.rejected: quote not found in the filing
